title: Large language model scoring of medical student reflection essays: Accuracy and reproducibility of prompt-model variations

live_model.evidence: Table 1: '2 outdated models (GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-3.5-Turbo) that are relevant for historical comparisons' ... 'Model: GPT-4-Turbo | 4-Turbo | None [As per Baseline]'

prompt.location: Table 1 footnote c (exact wording of the Baseline prompt) + Appendix Box 1 (rubric inserted verbatim)
prompt.note: GPT-4-Turbo condition = Baseline prompt with the model swapped; temperature 0.7; o4-mini condition identical.

claim.metric: mean absolute difference vs human reference score (MAD)
claim.location: Table 3, block 'GPT models, not fine-tuned', row B = GPT-4-Turbo (306 data points = 51 essays x 6 replications)

data.source: 15 real test essays from the 18 rater-training essays published with the O'Sullivan rubric + 36 essays generated with Gemini-2.0-flash (release not stated)

notes: Also reports o4-mini (MAD 0.55) and ICC-based accuracy/reproducibility. Reference scores are fixed human scores, so no judge is needed at re-run time. Soft gap: the 36 synthetic essays are not confirmed released.

resolution.plan: 15 of the 51 essays are the public O'Sullivan rater-training essays, but the 36 Gemini-generated essays and their reconciled reference scores appear only as a generation dialog (Appendix Table A1) and a score distribution (Table A2), not as text, so the 51-essay MAD cannot be recomputed; a 15-essay partial run would not be the paper's number.
